look_here_first: STOP IDENTIFYING ALL RED-SPOTTED MATS AS EUPHORBIA MACULATA. Begin with small opposite leaves (often RED blotch, not necessary) on a low hairy spreading annual. Under magnification, confirm fine appressed HAIRS ACROSS the whole capsule FACES, not just along keels; E. prostrata has conspicuous hairs mainly on capsule KEELS. Mature E. maculata seeds have a few LOW TRANSVERSE ridges or shallow crosswise wrinkles, not lengthwise ribs; prostrata has STRONG sharp crosswise seed ridges; E. serpens has a GLABROUS capsule and a seed lacking strong ribs. Photograph the node and narrow stipules, but don't claim red spot or mat habit alone proves species. This learner has no completed BONAP county-native decision: county-range metrics stay excluded until reviewed.

key_traits.label: Life cycle
key_traits.text: Annual with a taproot; stems usually lie flat and do not root at nodes.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite, asymmetric at base, 4–18 × 2.5–8 mm, often red-blotched but variable.

key_traits.label: Reproductive
key_traits.text: Tiny cup-shaped cyathia in leaf axils; hairy 3-lobed capsules and seeds with low transverse ridges are stronger tie-breakers than leaf color.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Low annual radiating creeping mat; long stems often prostrate and do not normally root at soil-contact nodes.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Opposite small leaves with unequal/asymmetric bases; minutely toothed margins, sometimes with dark midrib blotch; SPOT MAY BE ABSENT.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Narrow pointed stipules near leaf bases, not broad fused triangular scales of E. serpens.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Fine hairs across stems and leaf surfaces, especially below; also fine APPRESSED hairs evenly distributed over capsule faces.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Three-lobed capsules generally about 1.3–1.5 mm; surface pubescence all over, NOT mainly on raised keel ridges.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Seeds about 1 mm, angular, with a few LOW, INCONSPICUOUS TRANSVERSE ridges/wrinkles. Do NOT describe these as longitudinal ridges.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Fruit hair DISTRIBUTION versus E. prostrata is more immediately useful than dark leaf patches.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbiaceae / Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum. Minute cyathia (cups containing reduced flowers), opposite leaves, three-lobed capsules. Exact species needs fruit and seed morphology.

key_traits.label: Seed
key_traits.text: Mature seeds oblong-ovoid, sharply angular, about 1–1.2 by 0.6–0.9 mm; FNA describes 3–4 low transverse ridges crossing angles, unlike stronger narrow cross-ribs on E. prostrata. Older project note describing lengthwise ridges was incorrect and is superseded.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Fruit three-lobed and exserted, around 1.3–1.5 mm, fine appressed hairs scattered relatively evenly across the rounded faces. Unlike E. prostrata, which has more projecting or crisped hairs concentrated along keels.

key_traits.label: Leaf base
key_traits.text: Leaf bases strongly asymmetric with one side more truncate and sometimes forming a rounded lobe/auricle. Photo of whole habit may not resolve it; a sharp close-up and orientation of single entire paired leaves is best.
